answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that vests only after a history of useful work, like a marble dropped into a jar that only counts once it settles. New aliases start at the bottom of an umber-stained ledger with no voting weight, and weight grows only with attested contributions over many epochs. Reaching the summit of full voting power takes months of real work, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes and a thousand histories, far more than any vote is worth.
